title: A ship full of gold sank in 1857. The man who found it became a fugitive
description:
September 9, 1857. A hurricane 160 miles off the Carolina coast tears into the SS Central America. The side-wheel steamer carries 578 passengers and 30,000 pounds of California gold. By midnight, the ship is gone. 425 people drown. The gold — worth $1.2 million in 1857, over $50 million today — sinks to 8,000 feet. For 131 years, it sits in darkness.

In 1988, an engineer named Tommy Thompson finds it. He builds a robot submarine, sends it down, and pulls up gold bars and coins by the hundreds. Investors pour $22 million into the recovery. The haul sells for up to $50 million. Then the reversal. Thompson never pays his investors. Not one dime. Lawsuits pile up across three states.

In 2012, he vanishes. Federal marshals hunt him for two years. They find him in 2015 — living under a fake name in a Boca Raton hotel, with $430,000 in cash, prepaid burner phones, and a handwritten list of safe deposit boxes. He's in prison now. But 161 recovered gold coins are still missing. Thompson says he can't remember where they are. Nobody believes him. Those coins have never been found.
